result_semantic_payload.summary: The hypothesis that employee lihua exported the customer database on 2024-05-10 is NOT supported by the recorded evidence and is effectively refuted. The application log /export/app.log records the customer export at 2024-05-10 01:03:22 and 01:03:40 (status=success, duration=18s, dataset=customers, rows=184112, dest=/backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz) executed under account=svc_export, not lihua. Two corroborating artifacts establish that this was an automated scheduled job rather than a human action: (a) /export/app.log contains a preceding line at 2024-05-09 23:55:01 'SCHEDULE job=nightly_export account=svc_export triggered'; (b) /scheduler/jobs.conf defines a cron schedule 'schedule 23 = 55 daily' (23:55 daily), matching the trigger line to the minute. The README.txt describes svc_export as 'a dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs', i.e. it has no interactive login capability and cannot be an employee account. The only lihua activity in the evidence is two FAILED login attempts at 2024-05-10 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from ip=198.51.100.44 with reason=password; both failed, so lihua never obtained a session, and both attempts occurred ~44 minutes AFTER the export completed. Therefore the export was performed by the automated nightly_export job running as the service account svc_export. The lihua login failures are temporally adjacent to (but not causal of) the export and warrant separate attention as a possible credential-guessing / password-spray attempt against that account, but they do not link lihua to the export.

claim_candidates.text: The customer database export recorded on 2024-05-10 (EXPORT account=svc_export dataset=customers rows=184112 dest=/backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz at 01:03:22, status=success duration=18s at 01:03:40) was executed under the account svc_export, not under lihua.

The export was triggered by the scheduled job 'nightly_export': app.log shows 'SCHEDULE job=nightly_export account=svc_export triggered' at 2024-05-09 23:55:01, and /scheduler/jobs.conf defines a daily schedule at 23:55 ('schedule 23 = 55 daily').
svc_export is a dedicated non-interactive service account used by scheduled jobs, so it is not an employee login identity and could not have been used interactively by lihua.
The only lihua activity in the evidence is two login attempts on 2024-05-10 at 01:47:11 and 01:47:59 from ip=198.51.100.44, both FAILED with reason=password.

The hypothesis that employee lihua exported the customer database on 2024-05-10 is refuted by the evidence: no export event is attributed to lihua, lihua's only recorded activity consists of failed logins occurring ~44 minutes after the export completed, and the export is attributed to the automated nightly_export job running as svc_export.
limitations: Conclusion is bounded by the captured evidence set: /export/app.log is the only source recording EXPORT events, and no corroborating OS-level source (Windows Event Log, registry, prefetch/amcache) is present in this task, so the attribution rests on a single application log plus the scheduler definition.

claim_candidates.text: The two failed lihua logins from a single external IP shortly after the nightly export are consistent with credential guessing / password spraying against the lihua account, but the evidence does not establish intent, prior authorization, or any link to the export artifact.
limitations: No authentication source logs, no account lockout data, and no network flow data are available; reason=password alone does not distinguish a human typo, a stale credential, or automated guessing.

The 'windows' source scope contains no Windows artifacts in this task; the evidence is from a seized Linux-style application server, so Windows-specific verification (Event Log, registry, prefetch/amcache) was not possible.
Export attribution depends on a single application log (/export/app.log) plus the scheduler config; there is no independent OS-level corroboration of the export execution.

File timestamps are all equal to the capture timestamp (1790594134) and modified_time is null, so filesystem chronology cannot be used; chronology relies on in-log textual timestamps whose timezone is unspecified.
The export artifact /backup/customers_20240510.tar.gz is not present in the captured evidence and could not be inspected.
lihua's two failed logins are recorded only in the application log; without authentication source logs, intent and the origin host (198.51.100.44) cannot be characterized.
Log completeness cannot be verified (no rotation history or integrity baseline), so absence of a lihua-attributed export line is evidence of absence within the captured log only.
warnings: The analyst hypothesis is refuted by the available evidence; the export actor is the scheduled job nightly_export running as svc_export, not employee lihua.

The failed lihua logins from 198.51.100.44 immediately after the export may be coincidental but merit a separate credential-guessing investigation; they should not be treated as evidence of the export.
